authority: User asks for a complete single stage slide and then explicitly requests images here before Google Slides
google_slides: Deferred by direct user instruction; no remote file or sharing change performed
proof_scope: Analytical target-only cost baseline derived from recorded option calculations, compared with the recorded admissible plan; no new LLM baseline, model run or speed benchmark

variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Create ONE finished landscape 16:9 raster pitch slide, 1920x1080-like proportions, for AdaptOps. Full slide, no device, no surrounding frame. It will be the only slide visible on stage. Make it both complete and immediately understandable, with an elegant deliberate hierarchy and real whitespace.
Use exact brand and tagline:
"AdaptOps"
"Adapt as fast as your market changes."
One concise pitch:
"An agent that knows your business, coordinates a response and executes approved actions."

The audience should understand a company-level adaptation product, not a watch list or a small procurement assistant. The company report is ALREADY PREPARED from authorised company knowledge and sector events. The product identifies risks and opportunities, prepares ONE shared plan across procurement, operations, sales and finance, executes only approved actions within rights, verifies results, retains knowledge and reassesses. The timber/materials market is the first market, not the limit of the vision. The full connected-execution/opportunity loop remains a product target. Show it as a PRODUCT CONCEPT, not a screenshot of completed implementation.

A small, well-designed proposed product scene must convey this sequence using these concise exact labels:
"Your company brief is ready"
"ERP / CRM / WMS + prior research"
"Risks and opportunities"
"One coordinated plan"
"Procurement   Operations   Sales   Finance"
"Protect deliveries. Qualify new demand."
"Approve & execute"
"Verify results. Remember. Reassess."
Place the sources/storage caption naturally near the product scene:
"Public sources + company records. Evidence and memory in Aiven PostgreSQL."
This is the data layer: relevant external information + internal records + prior knowledge feed calculated options; decisions/results become durable memory. Do not turn this into a software architecture diagram.

Provide a genuinely legible proof area, with the following exact copy:
"SYNTHETIC DATA TEST"
"Lowest cost for A"
"€120 transfer"
"Leaves B uncovered"
"AdaptOps checks both"
"€1,420 purchase"
"Both commitments covered"
"Approved plan preserved after restart on Aiven."
Show a restrained comparison between a simple naive rule that chooses the cheapest way to cover A while ignoring other commitments, and the recorded admissible plan that checks both A and B. These are calculated outcomes in a synthetic case, not actual purchases or delivered goods. The €1,420 amount is a purchase COST, not savings. Do not label the baseline as a separately tested LLM or claim a measured time gain. Avoid a huge finance metric. This comparison is small evidence, not the central product promise.

Retain these three short pitch criteria, with readable supporting copy:
"WHO"
"Operations and procurement. Multi-site timber and materials first."
"WHY NOW"
"Agents combine research, business calculations and approved tool actions."
"FIRST USERS"
"Plan: recruit 3 design partners through founder introductions."
One single small readable scope note:
"Product vision. Synthetic test. No real purchase executed. Connected execution and opportunity loop pending."

Design:
White and very pale neutral, charcoal type, deep petrol teal and restrained mint. One refined sans-serif family like Inter. Strong typography with normal/medium/bold hierarchy, never giant extra-bold text everywhere. Subtle mint for a selected plan, subtle amber for a trade-off. Use native-looking editable-style UI fragments, but not a fake browser window with URL. No photo, no forest, no factory, no robot, no clipart, no decorative icons, no network spaghetti, no stock logos, no glow or loud gradient. No repeated wall of six cards. Main body around 24-30px at 1920-wide; proof labels and footer remain easily readable. Keep outer margins around 80-100px and useful space between groups.
Keep the whole slide polished and stage-readable, not dense. The brand, promise, prepared response and proof should be a clear reading sequence. All exact text above must fit without collisions. No new invented metrics, users, external domains, QR codes, or testimonials. English throughout, no em dash.
A tiny but unmistakable A, B or C badge goes in the top-right margin. Only this direction badge may be additional text. Do not add marketing paragraphs.

COMPOSITION A: EDITORIAL COMPANY RESPONSE, badge A.
Left 36%: AdaptOps brand, tagline in two/three beautifully balanced lines, and the short pitch, with generous negative space. Right 64%: one large, very clean company response view. Inside the view the brief/context sits at the top, the shared plan and four roles sit centrally, and the approval plus verification/memory sit at bottom. This is one coherent report, not isolated feature tiles. Beneath the main hero, a thin full-width proof strip compares the €120 transfer and €1,420 admissible option with enough text width to read. Bottom row holds WHO / WHY NOW / FIRST USERS and the scope note. Minimal petrol surfaces and open white space. Prioritise a premium investment-pitch composition over detailed dashboard UI.
